clue.text: About to rise, Henry makes a bloomer

indicators.note: About here means going round, so the name for Henry wraps around the verb

parts.note: Hal is the familiar short form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
to rise up against authority is to rebel

explanation.surface: Henry stands up and promptly makes an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but is a flowering plant; 'makes a' only links. 'to rise' is the verb sense, to revolt, not to stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is anything that flowers, and this bellflower is a wild plant with blue blossoms.

clue.text: Quickly and frequently turned up within call

indicators.note: within says the turned word sits inside the word for call

parts.note: a hoot is an owl's call

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: Something that happens quickly and often appears during a phone call.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reads a word bottom to top, so OFT becomes TFO before going inside the owl's call.
explanation.definitionFit: To go at speed, in haste, as if on burning feet.

clue.text: Furtively creep into party

indicators.note: furtively suggests sneaking about in a disguised way, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks stealthily into a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link but is fodder: 'Furtively' rearranges CREEP and INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal gathering, as for a wedding, is a social function.

clue.text: Blissful, without being retired

indicators.note: being retired is being in bed, so the word for without is placed in the bed

parts.note: to retire is to go to bed
less means without, as in 'a year less a day'

explanation.surface: Happy without having stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests leaving work, but here means gone to bed: LESS is in BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Blessed means divinely happy, in a state of heavenly joy.

clue.text: Still wearing former set of clothes

indicators.note: wearing says the word for former has the other word on, wrapped round it

parts.note: late means former, as in 'the late chairman'
yet means still, as in 'not yet'

explanation.surface: Someone still wearing an old outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete outfit of clothing and bedding prepared for a newborn baby.

clue.text: Tree that's vulgar, not posh

indicators.note: not says the letter for posh must be left out of the word for vulgar

parts.note: popular in its old sense of common, of the ordinary people
U is the old label for upper-class usage, so it stands for posh

explanation.surface: A tree described as common rather than refined.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class (as opposed to non-U) is a crossword convention; 'not' removes it from POPULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall, fast-growing deciduous tree is a common sight lining roads.

clue.text: Plenty in favour of union

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a fusion is a merging, a union

explanation.surface: A good deal in support of trade unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance, a great quantity of something.

clue.text: Soft and suitable for digging, that's the story

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
arable land is fit for ploughing and growing crops

explanation.surface: A tale about soil that is soft and easily worked.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple tale told to teach a moral, as in the Gospels.

clue.text: A suitor could become married

indicators.note: could become says the letters of married may be turned into another word

explanation.surface: A suitor might end up wedded.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who courts a person is a wooer.

clue.text: Satisfactory pass, yet at first express dissatisfaction

parts.note: a ticket is a pass that lets you in

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word yet

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone passes a test but still grumbles about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned British slang meaning fine, in good order, all going well.

clue.text: A capital ramble, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to ramble is to roam, wander aimlessly

explanation.surface: Someone praises a wonderful stroll, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' poses as the old British word for excellent; here it is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city is the seat of the country's government.

clue.text: Counterpart to 'pope' is, strangely, 'pop'

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of to, pope and is are oddly rearranged

parts.note: a pop song is a number, an item in a performance

explanation.surface: A riddle claiming the pontiff's opposite is a casual word for father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link but is fodder: TO, POPE and IS are rearranged to OPPOSITE by 'strangely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding the equivalent position in another body is one's equal across the table.

clue.text: Play with extremely smart theologian taken in by a trick

annotationWithheld.why: Play with extremely smart theologian taken in by a trick (7): parse is T + WI(DD)LE, but 'extremely smart' must give only T, the last letter of 'smart', while 'extremely' signals both ends (ST); no reading gives the single letter fairly
annotationWithheld.clue: Play with extremely smart theologian taken in by a trick

clue.text: When to feed and cultivate, mulch and tine

indicators.note: to cultivate soil is to turn it over, so the letters of mulch and tine are dug up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Gardening advice on feeding and working soil with mulch and a fork prong.
explanation.walkthrough: A tine is a prong of a garden fork; 'feed' suggests the plants, but means eat at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal hour is the time to eat.

clue.text: Piece of business holding the attention

indicators.note: holding says the business wraps around the word for attention

parts.note: a firm is a business company
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Part of a company's work keeps people's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' poses as a portion; in slang it is a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Piece is slang for a gun, the classic handheld weapon.

clue.text: Unkind remark like Xerxes, for instance, uttered

indicators.note: uttered says the phrase is to be spoken and heard, not spelt

parts.note: as Persian: Xerxes was a king of ancient Persia, so 'like' gives as and Xerxes an example of a Persian

explanation.surface: A rude comment, delivered as the Persian king might.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur, a damaging or derogatory comment.

clue.text: Bird pushing stuff

explanation.surface: A bird shoving some material around.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the bird, the verb bunt (to butt or push with the head) and flag fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A finch-like songbird; butting, as a goat or calf shoves; and the cloth used for festive flags.

clue.text: Arriviste puts a fresh interpretation on pictures

indicators.note: a fresh interpretation on means the word puts is read in a new way, with its letters reordered

parts.note: paintings and pictures are art

explanation.surface: A newcomer reinterprets paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: A social climber who has risen suddenly to wealth or status.

clue.text: Engineers follow their leader into the more remote scene of operations

annotationWithheld.why: Engineers follow their leader into the more remote scene of operations (7): only parse is TH(E)AT + RE, with E as the Engineers' own leader, so 'Engineers' gives both RE and the inserted E (one word, two jobs)
annotationWithheld.clue: Engineers follow their leader into the more remote scene of operations

clue.text: Cut and ran, having imbibed a small drink

indicators.note: having imbibed says the word for ran drinks in the small drink, holding it inside

parts.note: sped means ran, hurried
a nip is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone cut and ran after a quick drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Snipped is the past tense meaning trimmed with scissors.

clue.text: Mum, about to say more, is somewhat mournful

indicators.note: about says the word for mum goes round the other pieces

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence
to add is to say more, as in 'he added that...'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother about to speak further is a bit downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like mother, but means keep quiet, giving SH.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means rather, so this is rather sad or downcast.

clue.text: Mischievous child destroys looms

parts.note: an imp is a naughty child
to end something is to finish or destroy it

explanation.surface: A naughty child wrecks the weaving machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Looms here is a verb meaning threatens, hangs over as about to happen.

clue.text: Least shallow river has a bore

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
a pest is a nuisance, a bore

explanation.surface: The deepest river has a tidal wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' suggests a tidal wave on a river, fitting the surface; it means a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of deep: having the greatest depth.

clue.text: Plant into which James Hogg put his money?

definitions.text: Plant into which James Hogg put his money?

parts.words: Plant into which James Hogg put his money?
parts.note: James Hogg, the Scottish poet, was known as the Ettrick Shepherd, so his wallet would be a herdsman's purse, which also names a common weed

explanation.surface: A Scottish poet investing his money in a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: James Hogg (1770-1835) was a Scottish writer nicknamed the Ettrick Shepherd, Ettrick being a district of the Scottish Borders.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed of the cabbage family, named for its pouch-shaped seed pods.

clue.text: Tense but audible, gave instruction

indicators.note: audible says the word for gave instruction is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: taught means gave instruction, educated

explanation.surface: A nervous teacher who gave a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means stretched tight, tense like a rope under strain.

clue.text: From Bombay, a collection of papers one behind another

parts.note: Bombay, now Mumbai, is a city in India, so someone from there is Indian
a file is a folder of papers

explanation.surface: A folder of documents arriving from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking single file, each person directly behind the next, is the idiom.

clue.text: Goddess supplying just part of what he needed

indicators.note: just part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A goddess provides only some of what a man needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Goddess supplying just' as the definition; 'supplying' is a link and 'just part of' the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Horse in the ark a cob, perhaps

parts.note: an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant
a cob, or cobnut, is a kind of hazelnut, so an example of a nut

explanation.surface: A horse aboard Noah's ark, maybe a cob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cob' looks like a stocky horse, fitting the surface, but is a cobnut.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown horse is called by this colour name.
